Official BPR-max uses negative softmax weights \(w_j=\exp(s_j)/\sum_{k\in N}\exp(s_k)\) and per-example loss \(\ell=-\log[\sum_{j\in N}w_j\sigma(s_+-s_j)+10^{-24}]+\lambda\sum_{j\in N}w_js_j^2\). Thus regularization is the softmax-weighted squared negative score, outside the logarithm; `bpreg` defaults to **1.0**. Gradients flow through the weights. Scores include the configured final activation. Current official implementations sum example losses, then divide by configured batch size—even for a smaller final batch; there is no additional division by negative count. [Official Theano source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hidasib/GRU4Rec/master/gru4rec.py)

At each session-parallel step, every row scores the shared concatenation of batch targets and `n_sample` additional draws, sampled with replacement using training interaction frequency raised to `sample_alpha`. Theano defaults: 2,048 draws, exponent 0.75; official PyTorch defaults to exponent 0.5. Only the row’s diagonal target column is excluded: duplicate negatives retain multiplicity, and other columns containing the same positive ID remain negatives. No user-history exclusion occurs. [Official PyTorch source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hidasib/GRU4Rec_PyTorch_Official/master/gru4rec_pytorch.py)

Recommended adaptation, explicitly differing from native sampling: flatten valid next-item positions; build shared candidates, then mask per row by item ID, excluding padding, **every occurrence of its positive**, and all items in that user’s permitted training history, without consulting held-out labels. Preserve repeated positives as separate supervised events, including targets repeated in the prefix. For unique-item negatives, deduplicate candidate IDs before scoring; document this change because multiplicity changes softmax weighting. Normalize weights over remaining valid negatives; resample empty rows or omit them from both loss and denominator. Average losses over valid positions, with no further negative-count division. Use finite scores for regularization and explicit masks to avoid zero-times-infinity NaNs.
